q: The naive Bayes assumption is that attributes are:
options: Conditionally independent given the class
Independent of the class
All equally important in every dataset
Normally distributed
explain: Given the class, each attribute's probability does not depend on the others.

Without smoothing, a zero count causes which problem?
options: The whole product becomes zero, whatever the other evidence says
The class prior becomes one

q: Add-one smoothing: a word occurs 3 times in a class with 100 words in total, and the vocabulary has 50 words. Give P(word | class) to 3 decimal places.
Why add logarithms in a text classifier?
options: Multiplying many small probabilities underflows to zero
Logs make the classifier more naive
Logs remove the need for a prior
Logs make the counts whole numbers
explain: The sum of logs keeps the same ordering without underflow.

q: In the m-estimate, a larger m means:
options: The prior p is given more weight compared with the observed data
The observed data is given more weight
Probabilities can go below zero
Fewer classes are used
